There is already diverance between other chains, BNB and tron is movng towards -44 and near, canton has -65. Australia is moving towards requiring -78 for retail banks. If -44 falls off from use in five years, then we would deprecate the precompile and all contracts who switched to it would need to change?

Though teams position

> We want post-quantum verification available on-chain, and ML-DSA is the only current scheme mature enough to be considered. excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: The reason for 3 precompiles is to add all 3 strengths.  Some regulators are cool with ML-DSA-44, some want ML-DSA-65, and some are even requiring ML-DSA-87.  There is agreement on the algorithm, but the strength varies based on the country. The alternate is all three strengths in one precompile, but the logic is simpler if it's fixed algo not switched algo.

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content:
Going stronger just means bigger keys and signatures, no other restrictions.  It's not like P384 where the math wasn't friendly to the 256 bit registers and couldn't be done in-evm well (EVM384, pepridge farms remembers). 

One thing to note is that the ML-DSA digests are over the whole message, not a hash like ECDSA sigs.  However I expect auth sigs will be over the TXHash and I think that's fine, but a general purpose signer should support arbitrary message length (modulo gas)
